statcan.actual_title: Canadian Classification of Functions of Government (CCOFOG) by consolidated government component (x 1,000,000)
statcan.cited_title: Government finance statistics, statement of operations and balance sheet
statcan.universe: The table has only two components: 'Consolidated Canadian general government' and 'Consolidated provincial-territorial AND LOCAL governments (PTLG)'. There is no provincial-government-only series in this table. PTLG includes municipalities, school boards, hospitals and other health and social service institutions, and universities and colleges.
statcan.prov_only_table: 10-10-0024-01, Canadian classification of functions of government by general government component, does carry a provincial-and-territorial-governments component — but publishes only the 10 top-level COFOG divisions. Probing for 'Public debt transactions' and 'Transport' at that level returns no data.
statcan.latest_year: Reference year 2024, released 27 November 2025 ('Government spending by function, 2024'). Reference year 2023 corresponds to FY2023-24. The app is one full vintage stale.
statcan.comparability: StatCan's own documentation warns that inter-provincial comparisons are 'strictly impossible' for divisions where provinces delegate differently to municipalities.

social_ei.note: Employment Insurance is federal and essentially absent from provincial spending. The CCOFOG 'Unemployment' sub-function at the PTLG level is $262M for Ontario — 0.6% of its social protection and about 0.1% of total expense.
social_ei.composition: Composition also differs structurally between provinces. Of total social protection in 2024: sickness and disability was 33.3% in Ontario, 17.6% in Quebec and 50.7% in Alberta; family and children was 22.2% in Ontario, 42.3% in Quebec and 25.6% in Alberta. Quebec's subsidised childcare makes its social protection a different animal from Alberta's disability-dominated one.
